entities.summary: HD 183263 b is an extrasolar planet orbiting the star HD 183263. This planet has a minimum mass of 3.6 times more than Jupiter and takes 625 days to orbit the star. The planet was discovered on January 25, 2005 using multiple Doppler measurements of five nearby FGK main-sequence stars and subgiants obtained during the past 4–6 years at the Keck Observatory in Mauna Kea, Hawaii. These stars, namely, HD 183263, HD 117207, HD 188015, HD 45350, and HD 99492, all exhibit coherent variations in their Doppler shifts consistent with a planet in Keplerian motion, and the results were published in a paper by Geoffrey Marcy et al.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The discovery of HD 183263 b in 2005 marked a significant milestone in the search for exoplanets and our understanding of planetary formation. This finding has contributed to the development of new detection methods and expanded our knowledge of the diversity of planetary systems beyond our solar system.
